title: Manufacturing and Trade: Inventories and Sales (October 2026 data) — the business-inventories aggregate, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html re-fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial-research session (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 178 rows parsed independently of the proposal that discovered it). The row reads exactly "Manufacturing and Trade: Inventories and Sales | December 16, 2026 | 10:00 AM | October 2026", release code A202612161000, reference A202610, and it is the last MTIS row on the 2026 calendar. Corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (fetched 2026-09-06 at the live /-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/cqer/researchcq/gdpnow/ path), whose PostedUpdates sheet carries a 2026-12-16 10:00 row reading "Retail sales + inventories, Industrial production" — note that the Atlanta Fed never names MTIS separately, folding it into the "Retail sales + inventories" label. Stays estimate rather than flipping to CENSUS:-confirmed on the same three counts the sibling wholesale entry records: the lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep; this same Census page demonstrably carries Suspended rows (five Advance Economic Indicators reference months); and understating the label only widens caution on an event nothing licenses acting on. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The October-2026 business-inventories aggregate — the last of the three closers to the 2026-11-27 Advance Economic Indicators Report. DISCOVERED by the wholesale-trade-2026-12-09 initial-research sweep (proposals/mtis-2026-12-16.from-wholesale-trade-2026-12-09.json, now shadowed by this file); this canonical entry is written by the event's own initial research, which read that proposal first, upholds every claim in it, and adds three measured findings. THE COLLISION IS REAL AND PERMANENT: retail-sales-2026-12-16 is tracked, but it is the 08:30 Advance Monthly Retail Trade report for NOVEMBER data (A202612160830) — a different release, reference month and hour. Measured this session across eight Census calendar pages: MTIS has NEVER ONCE been released on a day without that advance retail report, 84 of 84 since 2019-11, so the two are structurally inseparable rather than coincidentally paired, and the calendar was tracking the loud half of the morning and missing the quiet half. Schedule record (measured, not asserted): 84 consecutive reference months 2019-11 through 2026-10 with ZERO suspensions, median 43-52 day lag (median 46, n=78); the 2025-26 lapse delayed it to +40d excess and it walked back monotonically over EIGHT editions (+40 -> +31 -> +29 -> +26 -> +19 -> +14 -> +6 -> -2), two more than the wholesale print needed, which is what a downstream aggregate looks like. So the 12-11 CR expiry does NOT expose the information, only the publication: all three of MTIS's inputs print inside the funded window (M3-2 full report 12-03 = 35.1% of the aggregate, Monthly Wholesale Trade 12-09 = 34.5%, and the retail 30.4% previewed by the 11-27 advance report), leaving 69.6% of the October aggregate already public before this release opens. Its GDPNow signature is the mirror image of the 12-09 print's: across the 79 MTIS vintages with a same-quarter delta, median |delta PCE| runs 0.3578pp against 0.0063pp on the other 1,743 (permutation p=0.00005) and median |delta GDP nowcast| 0.3717pp against 0.0860pp — the LOUDEST routine vintage in the archive — while |delta change-in-inventory-investment| runs 0.0529pp, and on 72 of 79 (91.1%) the PCE move exceeds the inventories move against a 57.9% base rate. The loudness is the 08:30 retail SALES number, not this report. Impact stays LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds: no house playbook is macro-keyed (grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md returns 0 hits, re-run 2026-09-06) and no instrument attaches. Two reading cautions belong with the entry rather than with a stance. Unlike its 12-09 sibling this edition's calendar configuration is ORDINARY, not novel: every December MTIS on record lands 1-3 days before quad witching (7 of 7), and 12-16 is two days before opex-2026-12-18. And Census's own MTIS announcements block states the 2023/2024 AIES benchmark reaches this report in TWO steps — retail restated in the 2026-10-15 edition, wholesale in the 2026-11-17 edition — while a Special Notice freezes M3 historical data and seasonal models for the remainder of 2026, so the 12-16 print is a mixed-vintage aggregate: two legs re-benchmarked, one leg frozen. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
